cells.place: Lingāla - Black stone (broken) lying in front of Śiva temple out side the village.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Lingāla situated in Kandūru mandala on the banks of the river Krishnā at Sōmāsila, by an individual named Tānda, son of Kanna-nāyaka and Mala-sāni. Further it states that the above mentioned individual established 3 shrines viz., of Vishnu in the name of Bhīmarāju, Śiva in the name of his own father and of Sūrya in the name of Gōkarnarāju in the village Kārupālu. (Published in H.A.S. Vol. 19, pp. 47-48.)

cells.place: Māmillapalli. - Do. (Second side) †
cells.date: Chālukya-Vikrama year 39, Plavaṅga, Mārgaśira ba. 6, Monday. Irregular
cells.remarks: Do. Records a gift (datti) of land situated at Māvindallapalli by Adisetti to god Nrsimha for food offerings. The gift land was purchased by Adisetti. Further it records the gift of some lands to god Nrisimha by Khēyadēva danadāṇyaka on the orders of the king. The gifts were made on the occasion of uttarāyana saṁkrānti (Ibid., page Nos. 63-64).

cells.date: Śaka 1220, Viļamba, Jyēshtha śu. 2, Monday = 1298 A.D., May 13, f.d.t. 75.

cells.place: Rāmājipalle. - Big pillar lying in front of Āñjanēyasvāmi temple.
cells.date: Śaka 971, Virōdhi, Bhādrapada ba. 12, Sunday = 1049 A.D., August 27.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the grant of 12 maţţars of land on the banks of Rāmēśvaratīrtha by Saṅkara-Gandarasar, the subordinate chief of the king Trailōkyamalla to the god Mahēśvaradēva for the maintenance and food offerings to the ascetics and brāhmaṇas. cells.date:
Chālukya-Vikrama year
9, Raktākshi,
Āśvayuja, Punnamē,
Lunar Eclipse =
1084 A.D.,
September 16.
cells.remarks: Refers to the administration of the chief mahā- mandalēśvara Jōyimarasu alias Edalēśvara Jōyimarasu over Edadōre-2000 and Kallakēla-500. At the instance of his subordinate Kallappayya, who was the maneverggade-danḍanāyaka, the chief granted land to god Śrī Kalidēvasvāmi of the Piriya-agrahāra of Gabbūr, for worship, khandasphuṭita and navakarma. The land was on the bank of a stream near the village Bādahalli, situated in Mudagundūru-70, and it was gifted as sarvvamāmya having the benefit of tribhōgābhyantara-siddhi. Further, it registers a few more grants by some other dignitaries (specified).

cells.remarks: Begins with the obeisance to Pārśva-prabhu and gives the genealogy of a line of Jaina pontiffs belonging to Mūla- saṁgha, Śāradā-gachchha, Valātkāra-gaṇa, Kundakund- ānvaya, mentioning the names of Bhaṭṭāraka Tribhuvanakīrti, Bhaṭṭāraka Sahaskarakīrti Bhaṭṭāraka Padmanandi, Bhaṭṭāraka Yaśaḥkīrti Bhaṭṭāraka Lalitākīrti and Bhaṭṭāraka Dharmakīrti in succession and records the perpetual obeisance of sādhu [Saraṇa] belonging to Paravār-ānvaya and Gōhīla-gōtra, his wife Niśā, their son, sarighapati Bhavānī[sa]dhan, Dhanha, his wife Yaśāmatī, Sahasamala, his wife Sōbhā, Vijayarāja, his wife Lājē, Raghōlaramala, his mother Kēsaritē and his wife Ghōshā, Chaturmani and his wife Pratīpade during the reign of Rāu Manōharadāsa. The kārigara was Bhavānī.

cells.remarks: Damaged. Begins with the praśasti portion referring to the merchant guild also referring to nāṇadeśi of Eripadai-nallūr in Tuvarāpati-nāḍu, aiññūṟuvan, nāṇgi diśaipppadinegbhūmi-diśaiyāyirratu-aiññūṟuvar, chettis of various mandalams, Dhamma-cheṭṭi and padinen-bhūmi Virakoḍiyār etc. Mentions Sembaiyan Sēnāpātyāṇḍan and Vaikuṇṭha-nādālvān alias Valangai-Vīra-gaṅga Pillai. In characters of about the 12th century A.D.

The verse portion states that Rājarāja Malādakularāyan, son of Tiruvan Semperiyan, of Vēlpūr, had constructed a stone temple for Śiva at Pudavūr, which delights those who see. It also records that he donated lands and made provisions for twilight lamps and also for flowers. He also donated land to the builder of the temple, Tillaināyaka-aliass Tillaināyaka-āchāriya. The prose portion states that Udaiyān Periyān Tiruvan alias Rājarāja Malāda-kularāyan, of Vēlpūr donated 1½ vēli of land in order to burn two perpetual lamps to the deity, Tiruvanantīsvaramudaiya-nāyanār in the temple of Pudavūr in Kīlnaraiyūr-kūrram (a sub-division) of Jananātha-valanādu (cf. No. 279 above).

cells.remarks: It begins with the usual praśasti 'tīngalēr tāru tēn tongal'. States that an individual Palliķķuttān Siyānāran Singalāntakap-Pēriyuvāriyan of Śēndankudi Mēlkā-nādu in Rājēndrasinha-valanādu, donated 30 cows to burn a perpetual lamp to the deity at Tirumudukunram. His younger brother Kūttādi Amatturayān Madhurāntakap-Pēriyuvāriyan donated another 32 cows for the same purpose. Eluvan-nādu-vallān alias Vayan Sundarapperiya araiyan. Eluvan-nādu-vallān alias Vayan Sundarap-periyarangan, Kaliyan alias Mudikoņda-chōla Muttaraiyan, Periyapān Vinnan Dēsavitanakan Piridhi and Perumān alias Kidārangonda-chōla Periyarāyan also donated 32 cows each for burning perpetual lamps to the same deity.

cells.remarks: Built-in. Contains the usual praśasti of the king ..... taṇakke urimai pūṇḍamai. It states that several persons Kāliyan, Araṇṭan Kaliyan and others of the village Kārikūḍal at Irungōlappādi in Rājēndrasiṅga-vaḷanāḍu sold their land as iraiyili-dēvadānam to the temple at Tirumudukuṉṛam. The land was also freed from taxes such as iṟai, echchōṟu, amañji, etc. The ūrār of Kārikūḍal themselves agreed to cultivate the land and agreed to measure out paddy as vāḍākkāḍan at the courtyard of the temple.

cells.location: LALGUDI TALUK Tinnakulam.
cells.place: South wall of the central shrine in the Tiruneruñjanāthar temple. North wall of the Viśvanātha shine in the same temple †
cells.king: Year 13, Mēsha ba. 12, Thursday, Pūraṭṭādi = 1179 A.D., April 5
cells.remarks: Damaged at the end. Records that some śivabrāhmaṇas of the 30 day cycle in the temple at Tiruneruṅkam migrated, while some did not. It appears that the amount of 438¼ kāśu earmarked for the expenses on offerings and worship to the deity were not entrusted earlier to those śivabrāhmaṇas who continued to reside in the village. Now they received the said amount and agreed to burn a perpetual lamp to the deity at Tiruneruṅkam in Poygaināḍu in Rājarāja-vaḻanāḍu. 32 cows and one bull were purchased with that amount to supply 91 nāli and 1 uḷakku of clarified butter for the lamp. The śivabrāhmaṇas gave an agreement to Uḍaiyār Rārājēdēvan of Pēḻaikuḍi and other temple officials to that effect.

cells.king: Year 13, Mēsha ba. 12, Thursday, Pūraṭṭādi = 1179 A.D., April 5
cells.remarks: Records that some śivabrāhmaṇas of the 30 day cycle, in Tiruppāḍaiśvaramudaiya-nāyaṇār temple at Madhurāntaka-chaturvēdimangalam migrated while some did not. Consequently worship in the temple ceased. Now the śivabrāhmaṇas who remained entered into an agreement with the temple official Ponnambala-nambi, mendicant Araiya Dēvāṇḍan, temple official Tiruchchhirgambala-bhaṭṭan and the temple accountant Mūvalūr-uḍaiyār.

cells.location: VILLUPURAM TALUK Alür.
cells.place: On the south wall of the garbhagriha in the temple of Tiruvālisvaramudaiyār
cells.remarks: Refers to the collection of taxes kadamai etc. from the kāśāyakkudi residing in and around the temple precincts by the kōyil-tāpattar for the maintenance of pūjā and repairs (tiruppani) in the temple of Tiruvālandurai-udaiya nāyanar. Further it states that the new settlement of weavers as (kāśāyakkudi) to be settled in the village from the 19th regnal year onwards should pay the taxes such as kadamai, sūlavari, vāsalpanam, pörkkadami nālāyam and the same would be sarvamānya of the temple for the day to day expenditure. In characters of the 13th century A.D.
